title: As a founder, I can issue physical and virtual corporate cards to the team in minutes, each with its own spend limit
As a finance lead, I can restrict cards by category, merchant, and amount — and the platform auto-locks or declines out-of-policy spend at the point of sale
As a finance lead, I can create single-vendor virtual cards for SaaS subscriptions and procurement so one compromised vendor never exposes shared credit
As an employee, I can snap a photo or forward an email and the platform OCRs the receipt and files it against the right transaction
As an employee, receipts match to card transactions automatically — with e-receipts pulled from integrations — and I get nudged only when one is genuinely missing
As an employee, I can log mileage with map-based distance and claim per-diem rates without building the expense by hand
As a finance lead, I can codify our expense policy — limits by category, role, and context — so in-policy expenses auto-approve and only exceptions reach a human
As a finance lead, I can build multi-step approval chains — manager, budget owner, finance — with delegation and escalation when approvers sit on requests
As a finance lead, every expense carries a full audit trail — edits, approvals, policy checks — that survives an external audit
As an employee, I can submit an out-of-pocket expense and get reimbursed by direct deposit in days, tracked from submission to payout
As a finance lead, I can reimburse employees abroad in their local currency without running a separate international payments process
As a finance lead, transactions sync to QuickBooks, NetSuite, or Xero with GL account, class, and department mappings I control
As a finance lead, spend is coded as it happens — merchant, category, memo, receipt — so month-end close is a review, not an archaeology dig
As a finance lead, I can run multiple legal entities and currencies in one account with consolidated reporting and per-entity books
As an employee, I can book flights and hotels in-platform with travel policy applied at booking time, not expensed and argued about later
As an employee, a trip's expenses — bookings, cards, receipts — collect themselves into one itinerary-linked report
As a founder, I can see company spend in real time — by team, category, and merchant — the day it happens, not when statements land
As a finance lead, I can allocate budgets to teams and projects and have card limits and approvals actually enforce them
As a finance lead, I can run accounts payable in the same platform — capture invoices, route approvals, and pay vendors by ACH, check, or wire
As a developer, I can pull transactions, expenses, and receipts through a documented REST API with OAuth and scoped tokens
As a developer, I can issue and manage cards programmatically — create a card with a limit, lock it, update controls — via the public API
As an AI-native user, an agent can pull uncoded transactions via API or MCP, propose categorizations and policy flags, and push clean coding back for review
As an AI-native user, AI codes and audits expenses for me — reading receipts, suggesting categories and memos, and catching duplicates or fraud
As an AI-native user, an AI assistant enforces policy conversationally — chasing missing receipts, explaining declines, and answering "can I expense this?" before the spend happens
